intro: Hi! In this lesson you'll learn phrasal verbs: a verb + a small word, like get up, turn on, put on and look for. You'll use them at home and to talk about your day, and you'll learn to guess their meaning from the sentence. Warm-up: what time do you get up?
teachingNotes: A phrasal verb is a verb + a small word (up, on, off, out, back, for, down) that together have a new meaning: get = mendapat, but get up = bangun dari tempat tidur; look = melihat, but look for = mencari. Teach each one as a whole chunk, like a new word, never word by word. Learners already met sit down, stand up (A0), wake up, get up (A1 daily routines) and turn on your camera / the AC (A0, A1): use them as a bridge.

Common errors: *'Please open the light' / 'close the TV' (Indonesian buka/tutup lampu) → turn on / turn off (switch on / off is also correct, common in British English); *'open your shoes' (buka sepatu) → take off; *'I'm looking my keys' (mencari has no extra word) → looking for; *'It's cold. Put on it.' → Put it on; *'She get ups' → she gets up: the -s goes on the verb, not on the small word. Negatives and questions as in the simple present: doesn't get up, What time do you get up?

Where the thing goes: with turn on/off, put on, take off and pick up the noun can go after the small word or in the middle (turn on the light = turn the light on). With it / them (and me, him, her) only in the middle: turn it on, pick them up, never 'turn on it'. look for is the exception: it never splits (look for it, never 'look it for'). Present it as something to remember; don't use the words separable / inseparable with the learner. wake up, get up, go out, come back, sit down and stand up have no thing after them in this lesson (don't teach 'wake someone up').

Meaning from context: the words around help (light, TV, AC, fan → on/off; clothes, shoes, helmet → put on / take off; can't find → look for). pick up has several meanings that only the context shows: pick up a pen (mengambil), pick up the phone (mengangkat), pick up my son from school (menjemput). Indonesian 'pakai' is both put on (the action: I put on my helmet) and wear (have it on: I'm wearing a helmet); mention it, don't drill it.

Limits: present simple, present continuous, imperatives and can only. No past simple (got up, turned off), no will, no going to, no present perfect. Don't add more phrasal verbs (find out, look after, give up, turn up / down, get on) or three-word ones; keep to the sets in the lesson.

keyPoints.title: Everyday phrasal verbs at home
keyPoints.explanation: A phrasal verb is a verb + a small word with a new meaning. At home: turn on / turn off (menyalakan / mematikan: the light, TV, AC), put on / take off (memakai / melepas: clothes, shoes, a helmet), look for (mencari), pick up (mengambil, menjemput). Lights and TVs are not 'opened' or 'closed': turn them on or off. The thing can go in the middle (turn the light on), but it / them must go in the middle: put it on, not 'put on it'. look for never splits: look for it.

examples.en: It's dark in here. Can you turn on the light?
examples.id: Di sini gelap. Bisa nyalakan lampunya?

examples.en: Here's your jacket. Put it on.

id.title: Phrasal verb sehari-hari di rumah
id.explanation: Phrasal verb adalah kata kerja + kata kecil yang punya arti baru. Di rumah: turn on / turn off (menyalakan / mematikan: lampu, TV, AC), put on / take off (memakai / melepas: baju, sepatu, helm), look for (mencari), pick up (mengambil, menjemput). Lampu dan TV tidak di-'open' atau di-'close': pakai turn on atau turn off. Bendanya boleh di tengah (turn the light on), tapi it / them harus di tengah: put it on, bukan 'put on it'. look for tidak pernah dipisah: look for it.

keyPoints.title: Guess the meaning from the context
keyPoints.explanation: The words around a phrasal verb help you guess what it means. A light, a TV or a fan → on / off. Clothes, shoes or a helmet → put on / take off. 'I can't find ...' → look for. One phrasal verb can have more than one meaning, and the sentence tells you which: pick up a pen (mengambil), pick up the phone (mengangkat), pick up your son from school (menjemput).

examples.en: Budi gets home and takes off his shoes.
examples.id: Budi sampai di rumah dan melepas sepatunya.

examples.en: The phone is ringing. Can you pick it up?
Bu Ani picks up her son from school at two.
examples.id: Bu Ani menjemput anaknya dari sekolah jam dua.

id.title: Menebak arti dari konteks
id.explanation: Kata-kata di sekitar phrasal verb membantumu menebak artinya. Lampu, TV atau kipas → on / off. Baju, sepatu atau helm → put on / take off. 'I can't find ...' (saya tidak bisa menemukan ...) → look for. Satu phrasal verb bisa punya lebih dari satu arti, dan kalimatnya yang memberi tahu arti yang mana: pick up a pen (mengambil), pick up the phone (mengangkat), pick up your son from school (menjemput).

keyPoints.title: Your day with phrasal verbs
keyPoints.explanation: wake up = bangun (membuka mata), get up = bangun dari tempat tidur, go out = keluar rumah, pergi main, come back = kembali, pulang. They use the simple present for routines. With he / she the -s goes on the verb, not on the small word: she gets up, he comes back (never 'get ups'). Negative: I don't get up early on Sundays. Question: What time do you get up?

examples.en: I wake up at 4:30, but I get up at five.
examples.id: Saya bangun jam setengah lima, tapi baru turun dari tempat tidur jam lima.

examples.en: My father comes back from the office at six.
examples.id: Ayah saya pulang dari kantor jam enam.

examples.en: Rina goes out with her friends on Saturdays.
examples.id: Rina pergi main dengan teman-temannya setiap Sabtu.

id.title: Rutinitasmu dengan phrasal verb
id.explanation: wake up = bangun (membuka mata), get up = bangun dari tempat tidur, go out = keluar rumah, pergi main, come back = kembali, pulang. Untuk rutinitas, pakai simple present. Dengan he / she, -s ditaruh di kata kerjanya, bukan di kata kecilnya: she gets up, he comes back (jangan pernah 'get ups'). Negatif: I don't get up early on Sundays. Pertanyaan: What time do you get up?

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with on or off: It's very hot in here. Can you turn ___ the fan, please?
guidedPractice.hint: It's hot, so you want the fan to work: turn it on.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: Here's your helmet. Put on it.
expected: here's your helmet put it on
here is your helmet put it on
heres your helmet put it on
guidedPractice.hint: With it, the small word goes after it: put it on.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete: Pak Hasan can't find his glasses. He's looking ___ them.
guidedPractice.hint: mencari = look for. Don't forget the small word.

guidedPractice.prompt: Read: 'Sari turns off the lights before she goes to bed.' What does 'turns off' mean in Indonesian?
guidedPractice.hint: She goes to bed, so the room needs to be dark.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'come back': Budi ___ home at seven every evening.
guidedPractice.hint: Budi = he, so the -s goes on the verb: comes back.

independentPractice.prompt: Write two sentences about your morning with wake up and get up.
independentPractice.hint: I wake up at ... . I get up at ... .

independentPractice.prompt: What do you do when you get home? Write one sentence with take off or turn on.
independentPractice.hint: For example: I take off my shoes ... / I turn on the fan ...

independentPractice.prompt: Read: 'Rina puts on her helmet and starts her motorbike.' Is her helmet on her head now? Write yes or no.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Please close the TV. Nobody is watching it.
acceptableAnswers: please turn off the tv nobody is watching it
please turn the tv off nobody is watching it
please switch off the tv nobody is watching it
please switch the tv off nobody is watching it
assessment.rubric: Correct: Please turn off the TV (or turn the TV off; switch off is also correct). Nobody is watching it. 'Please turn off' without the TV = 60. 'turn on' = 0 (wrong meaning). 'shut the TV' = 0 (same trap as close). The sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Put the words take, them and off in the right order: Your shoes are dirty. Please ___ before you come in.
assessment.rubric: Correct: take them off. 'take off them' = 0 (with them, the small word goes after them). 'take off' without them = 40.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: I'm looking my glasses. Can you help me?
acceptableAnswers: i'm looking for my glasses can you help me
i am looking for my glasses can you help me
im looking for my glasses can you help me
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'm looking for my glasses. Can you help me? 'I'm looking at my glasses' = 0 (look at = melihat, not mencari). 'I'm looking my glasses for' = 20 (look for never splits). The sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Read: 'Dimas wakes up at 5:00, but he gets up at 5:30.' At 5:15, is Dimas still in bed? Write yes or no.
assessment.rubric: Correct: yes. At 5:15 his eyes are open (he wakes up at 5:00), but he leaves the bed only at 5:30 (get up). 'no' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Read: 'Bu Ani goes out at seven every evening and comes back at eight.' Where is she at nine: at home or out?
assessment.rubric: Correct: at home. She comes back (pulang) at eight, so at nine she is at home again. 'out' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with 'get up' in the negative: On Sundays, my husband ___ before nine.
assessment.rubric: Correct: doesn't get up. 'don't get up' = 50 (my husband = he → doesn't). 'doesn't gets up' = 50 (after doesn't, no -s). 'not get up' = 20. 'doesn't get' without up = 30.

assessment.prompt: Complete Budi's routine with a phrasal verb: 'I get home at six. I ___ my work clothes and have a shower.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: take off. 'put on' = 0 (wrong meaning: before a shower you take your clothes off). 'open' = 0 (Indonesian 'buka baju' is take off in English). 'takes off' = 60 (I → take, no -s).

blocks.text: A **phrasal verb** is a **verb** (an action word, like *get, look, turn, put*) + a **small word** like *up, on, off, out, back, for, down*. Together they make a **new meaning**, often very different from the verb alone. So **don't translate them word by word**: *get* = mendapat and *up* = ke atas, but **get up** = bangun dari tempat tidur, not 'mendapat ke atas'. Learn each phrasal verb as a whole, like a new word. Good news: you already know some! *Sit down, stand up, wake up, get up, turn on your camera*.

id.text: **Phrasal verb** adalah **kata kerja** (kata untuk kegiatan, seperti *get, look, turn, put*) + **kata kecil** seperti *up, on, off, out, back, for, down*. Bersama-sama mereka punya **arti baru**, sering sangat berbeda dari kata kerjanya sendiri. Jadi **jangan diterjemahkan kata per kata**: *get* = mendapat dan *up* = ke atas, tapi **get up** = bangun dari tempat tidur, bukan 'mendapat ke atas'. Hafalkan setiap phrasal verb secara utuh, seperti kosakata baru. Kabar baiknya: kamu sudah kenal beberapa! *Sit down, stand up, wake up, get up, turn on your camera*.

rows.en: get → get up
look → look for
turn → turn on
put → put on
sit → sit down
rows.note: almost the same: down just adds 'ke bawah'

id.note: hampir sama: down hanya menambah 'ke bawah'

blocks.text: Why is **sit down** almost the same as *sit*, but **get up** very different from *get*? Some phrasal verbs are easy to guess (*sit down, stand up, come back*), others are not (*get up, look for, turn on*). You can't always see the meaning in the two words, so just **learn them like new words**.

id.text: Kenapa **sit down** hampir sama dengan *sit*, tapi **get up** sangat berbeda dari *get*? Ada phrasal verb yang mudah ditebak (*sit down, stand up, come back*), ada yang tidak (*get up, look for, turn on*). Artinya tidak selalu kelihatan dari dua katanya, jadi **hafalkan saja seperti kosakata baru**.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence has a phrasal verb?
options: I get a message from Rina.
I get a taxi to the station.
blocks.explain: get up = verb + small word with a new meaning (bangun dari tempat tidur). In the other two sentences get is alone (get a message = menerima pesan, get a taxi = naik taksi).

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang punya phrasal verb?
id.explain: get up = kata kerja + kata kecil dengan arti baru (bangun dari tempat tidur). Di dua kalimat lainnya get berdiri sendiri (get a message = menerima pesan, get a taxi = naik taksi).

material.title: Your day: wake up, get up, go out, come back

blocks.text: Four phrasal verbs for your routine. **wake up** = bangun (your eyes open). **get up** = bangun dari tempat tidur (you leave the bed). Indonesian *bangun* is both, but English has two: *I wake up at 4:30, but I get up at five.* **go out** = keluar rumah, pergi main (often for fun: with friends, to eat). **come back** = kembali, pulang. These four have **no thing right after them**: you can add a time or a place with a small word (*get up **at** six, come back **from** the office*), but never 'I get up the bed'. For routines, use the **simple present**, as you know.

id.text: Empat phrasal verb untuk rutinitasmu. **wake up** = bangun (matamu terbuka). **get up** = bangun dari tempat tidur (kamu meninggalkan kasur). Bahasa Indonesia hanya punya *bangun*, tapi bahasa Inggris punya dua: *I wake up at 4:30, but I get up at five.* **go out** = keluar rumah, pergi main (sering untuk bersenang-senang: dengan teman, untuk makan). **come back** = kembali, pulang. Keempatnya **tidak langsung diikuti benda**: kamu boleh menambah waktu atau tempat dengan kata kecil (*get up **at** six, come back **from** the office*), tapi jangan pernah 'I get up the bed'. Untuk rutinitas, pakai **simple present**, seperti yang sudah kamu tahu.

rows.en: I wake up at 4:30, but I get up at five.
rows.id: Saya bangun jam setengah lima, tapi baru turun dari tempat tidur jam lima.

rows.en: Rina goes out with her friends on Saturdays.
rows.id: Rina pergi main dengan teman-temannya setiap Sabtu.

rows.en: My father comes back from the office at six.
rows.id: Ayah saya pulang dari kantor jam enam.

rows.en: I don't go out on weekdays.
rows.id: Saya tidak pergi main di hari kerja.

rows.en: What time do you get up?

blocks.text: With **he / she / one person**, the **-s goes on the verb**, not on the small word: she **gets up**, he **comes back**, Rina **goes out**. Never 'she get ups'. Negative and question work like every simple present verb: she **doesn't get up**, **does** he **come back** at six?

id.text: Dengan **he / she / satu orang**, **-s ditaruh di kata kerjanya**, bukan di kata kecilnya: she **gets up**, he **comes back**, Rina **goes out**. Jangan pernah 'she get ups'. Negatif dan pertanyaan sama seperti kata kerja simple present lainnya: she **doesn't get up**, **does** he **come back** at six?

blocks.explain: Rina = she, so the verb takes -s: gets up. The small word up never changes.

id.explain: Rina = she, jadi kata kerjanya diberi -s: gets up. Kata kecil up tidak pernah berubah.

id.title: Harimu: wake up, get up, go out, come back

material.title: At home: turn on, put on, look for, pick up

blocks.text:
Phrasal verbs you use at home every day:
- **turn on / turn off** = menyalakan / mematikan: the light, the TV, the AC, the fan, your phone.
- **put on / take off** = memakai / melepas: clothes, shoes, a helmet, a mask.
- **look for** = mencari: your keys, your phone.
- **pick up** = mengambil (from the floor or a table), menjemput (a person).
You can also say **switch on / switch off**: same meaning, very common in British English.

id.text:
Phrasal verb yang kamu pakai di rumah setiap hari:
- **turn on / turn off** = menyalakan / mematikan: lampu, TV, AC, kipas, HP.
- **put on / take off** = memakai / melepas: baju, sepatu, helm, masker.
- **look for** = mencari: kunci, HP.
- **pick up** = mengambil (dari lantai atau meja), menjemput (orang).
Kamu juga bisa bilang **switch on / switch off**: artinya sama, sangat umum di bahasa Inggris British.

rows.en: It's hot. Turn on the AC, please.
Turn off your phone in the cinema.
It's raining. Put on your jacket!
We take off our shoes at the door.
rows.id: Kami melepas sepatu di depan pintu.

rows.en: Budi is looking for his keys.
I pick up my daughter from school at one.
rows.id: Saya menjemput anak perempuan saya dari sekolah jam satu.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: we say *buka / tutup lampu* or *buka sepatu*. In English **open / close** is for doors, windows, shops and books. For a light, TV, AC or fan: **turn on / turn off**, not 'open the light'. For clothes and shoes: **take off**, not 'open your shoes'.

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: kita bilang *buka / tutup lampu* atau *buka sepatu*. Dalam bahasa Inggris **open / close** dipakai untuk pintu, jendela, toko dan buku. Untuk lampu, TV, AC atau kipas: **turn on / turn off**, bukan 'open the light'. Untuk baju dan sepatu: **take off**, bukan 'open your shoes'.

blocks.text: *Mencari* is one word in Indonesian, so many learners say 'I'm looking my keys'. In English you need **for**: I'm looking **for** my keys. Without *for*, **look** means *melihat*, and **look at** = melihat ke (*Look at the board*).

id.text: *Mencari* hanya satu kata dalam bahasa Indonesia, jadi banyak orang bilang 'I'm looking my keys'. Dalam bahasa Inggris perlu **for**: I'm looking **for** my keys. Tanpa *for*, **look** artinya *melihat*, dan **look at** = melihat ke (*Look at the board*).

blocks.text: *Pakai* has two English words. **put on** is the action, the moment you put it on your body: *I put on my helmet and go.* **wear** means you have it on: *Rina is wearing a red dress.* In this lesson we practise **put on**.

id.text: *Pakai* punya dua kata dalam bahasa Inggris. **put on** adalah kegiatannya, saat kamu memasangnya di badan: *I put on my helmet and go.* **wear** artinya sedang kamu pakai: *Rina is wearing a red dress.* Di pelajaran ini kita berlatih **put on**.

blocks.prompt: Budi can't find his keys. He's ___ them.
blocks.explain: mencari = look for: He's looking for them. 'looking them' has no for, and 'looking at' = melihat ke, but he can't see them.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Budi can't find his keys. He's ___ them.
id.explain: mencari = look for: He's looking for them. 'looking them' tidak punya for, dan 'looking at' = melihat ke, padahal dia tidak bisa melihat kuncinya.

id.title: Di rumah: turn on, put on, look for, pick up

blocks.text: With **turn on / off, put on, take off** and **pick up**, the thing can go **after** the small word or **in the middle**. Both are correct and mean the same: *turn on the light* = *turn the light on*. But when the thing is **it** or **them** (short words that replace a thing: *it* = itu, -nya; *them* = mereka, -nya), it must go **in the middle**: turn **it** on, put **them** on. Never 'turn on it' or 'put on them'. The same for **me, him, her**: *I pick him up at two.*

id.text: Dengan **turn on / off, put on, take off** dan **pick up**, bendanya boleh di **belakang** kata kecil atau **di tengah**. Keduanya benar dan artinya sama: *turn on the light* = *turn the light on*. Tapi kalau bendanya **it** atau **them** (kata pendek pengganti benda: *it* = itu, -nya; *them* = mereka, -nya), harus **di tengah**: turn **it** on, put **them** on. Jangan pernah 'turn on it' atau 'put on them'. Begitu juga dengan **me, him, her**: *I pick him up at two.*

rows.en: Turn on the fan. = Turn the fan on.
The fan? Turn it on.
Put your shoes on. = Put on your shoes.
Your shoes? Put them on.
I'm looking for my bag. I'm looking for it.
rows.id: Saya sedang mencari tas saya. Saya sedang mencarinya.

blocks.text: **look for** is an **exception**: it never splits. The thing always goes after *for*: look for **my bag**, look for **it**. Never 'look it for' or 'look my bag for'. There's no rule you can see here, so just remember it. *wake up, get up, go out, come back, sit down* and *stand up* have no thing right after them, so there is nothing to move.

id.text: **look for** adalah **pengecualian**: tidak pernah dipisah. Bendanya selalu di belakang *for*: look for **my bag**, look for **it**. Jangan pernah 'look it for' atau 'look my bag for'. Tidak ada aturan yang kelihatan di sini, jadi hafalkan saja. *wake up, get up, go out, come back, sit down* dan *stand up* tidak langsung diikuti benda, jadi tidak ada yang perlu dipindah.

blocks.prompt: The lamp is on, but nobody is in the room. Which is correct?
blocks.explain: With it, the small word goes after it: Turn it off. 'Turn off it' is a common mistake, and 'Turn it' has no off, so it doesn't mean mematikan.

id.prompt: Lampunya menyala, tapi tidak ada orang di kamar. Mana yang benar?
id.explain: Dengan it, kata kecilnya ditaruh setelah it: Turn it off. 'Turn off it' adalah kesalahan yang sering terjadi, dan 'Turn it' tidak punya off, jadi artinya bukan mematikan.

material.title: Guess the meaning from the context

blocks.text:
When you meet a phrasal verb, look at the **context**: the words and the situation around it. They often tell you the meaning:
- a light, TV, AC, fan → **on / off**
- clothes, shoes, a helmet, a mask → **put on / take off**
- *I can't find ...* → **look for**
- a time and a place: *at seven ... at eight* → **go out / come back**
Some phrasal verbs have **more than one meaning**, and only the context tells you which. **pick up** is a good example.

id.text:
Saat kamu bertemu phrasal verb, lihat **konteksnya**: kata-kata dan situasi di sekitarnya. Itu sering memberi tahu artinya:
- lampu, TV, AC, kipas → **on / off**
- baju, sepatu, helm, masker → **put on / take off**
- *I can't find ...* (saya tidak bisa menemukan ...) → **look for**
- jam dan tempat: *at seven ... at eight* → **go out / come back**
Ada phrasal verb yang punya **lebih dari satu arti**, dan hanya konteksnya yang memberi tahu arti yang mana. **pick up** adalah contoh yang bagus.

rows.en: There's a pen on the floor. Can you pick it up?
rows.id: Ada pulpen di lantai. Bisa tolong ambil?

rows.en: The phone is ringing. Can you pick it up?
rows.note: pick up the phone = mengangkat telepon

id.note: pick up the phone = mengangkat telepon

rows.en: Bu Ani picks up her son from school at two.
rows.id: Bu Ani menjemput anaknya dari sekolah jam dua.

rows.en: Budi gets home and takes off his shoes.
rows.id: Budi sampai di rumah dan melepas sepatunya.

blocks.text: Don't stop at a word you don't know. Read the whole sentence and ask: **what is the person doing with the thing?** *Sari is cold. She puts on a jacket.* Cold + jacket → she is wearing it now: **put on** = memakai.

id.text: Jangan berhenti di kata yang tidak kamu tahu. Baca seluruh kalimatnya dan tanya: **orang itu sedang melakukan apa dengan bendanya?** *Sari is cold. She puts on a jacket.* Dingin + jaket → sekarang jaketnya dia pakai: **put on** = memakai.

blocks.prompt: Read: 'Pak Hasan picks up his daughter from school at one.' What does he do at one?
options: He goes to the school, and they go home together.
He calls his daughter on the phone.
He looks at a photo of his daughter.
blocks.explain: pick up + a person + from school = menjemput: he goes there and they go home together. The context (a person, from school) tells you the meaning.

id.prompt: Baca: 'Pak Hasan picks up his daughter from school at one.' Apa yang dia lakukan jam satu?
id.explain: pick up + orang + from school = menjemput: dia ke sana dan mereka pulang bersama. Konteksnya (orang, dari sekolah) memberi tahu artinya.

suggestedQuestions: What's the difference between wake up and get up?
Why can't I say 'open the light'?
Why is it 'put it on' but 'look for it'?
Is 'switch on' the same as 'turn on'?

id.note: Halaman level B1–B2, di atas level pelajaran ini. Baca bagian pertamanya: bendanya boleh di tengah atau di belakang, tapi it / them harus di tengah. Ada dua tes singkat.

flashcards.front: keluar rumah, pergi main / kembali, pulang

flashcards.back: turn on the light / turn off the light

id.intro: Hai! Di pelajaran ini kamu akan belajar phrasal verb: kata kerja + kata kecil, seperti get up, turn on, put on dan look for. Kamu akan memakainya di rumah dan untuk menceritakan harimu, dan kamu akan belajar menebak artinya dari kalimat. Pemanasan: kamu bangun jam berapa?
suggestedQuestions: Apa bedanya wake up dan get up?
Kenapa tidak boleh bilang 'open the light'?
Kenapa 'put it on' tapi 'look for it'?

assessment.pv-1: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Please close the TV. Nobody is watching it.
assessment.pv-2: Susun kata take, them dan off dengan urutan yang benar: Your shoes are dirty. Please ___ before you come in.
assessment.pv-3: Perbaiki kesalahannya: I'm looking my glasses. Can you help me?
assessment.pv-4: Baca: 'Dimas wakes up at 5:00, but he gets up at 5:30.' Jam 5:15, apakah Dimas masih di tempat tidur? Tulis yes atau no.
assessment.pv-5: Baca: 'Bu Ani goes out at seven every evening and comes back at eight.' Jam sembilan dia di mana: at home atau out? Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.pv-6: Lengkapi dengan 'get up' dalam bentuk negatif: On Sundays, my husband ___ before nine.
assessment.pv-7: Lengkapi rutinitas Budi dengan phrasal verb: 'I get home at six. I ___ my work clothes and have a shower.'
